title: Sledding in Berlin - FAQ
subtitle: Snow data from the Dahlem weather station, 31 winters, checked on 27 October 2026.

items.q: How much snow do you need for sledding in Berlin?
items.a: My rule: **5 cm is a thin run** on a short, steep slope and **10 cm is a proper day**. The threshold is my judgment, not an official figure. Under 3 cm is a dusting and not worth the trip.

items.q: How often is there enough snow for sledding in Berlin?
items.a: Not often. At the Dahlem station, **22 of 31 winters** had at least one weekend day with 5 cm of snow or more, but only **9 of 31** had one with 10 cm. The typical winter gave **2 weekend days at 5 cm** and none at 10 cm.

items.q: Which month is best for sledding in Berlin?
items.a: January and February. Of the **124 weekend days** since 1995/96 with 5 cm or more, **80 fell in January and February**, 24 in December, 18 in March and 2 in November.

items.q: How long does the snow stay?
items.a: Not long. Spells with 5 cm or more had a median length of **3 days**, and **46 per cent lasted two days or less**. If the forecast gives 5 cm, go the first morning.

items.q: Which hill is best for small children?
items.a: The flatter run-out in **Volkspark Prenzlauer Berg** or the small **Bunkerberg** in Volkspark Friedrichshain. Teufelsberg is long and fast and better for older children and adults.

The old official run is closed and partly fenced off, according to the Wikipedia article on the hill, and people sled and snowboard there anyway. I could not find a district rule either way, so read the signs on the day.

items.q: Are there official sledding runs in Berlin?
items.a: In Mitte, no. In July 2021 the Bezirksamt wrote that **sledding runs are no longer designated** in the district's parks and that the places people use are repaired in autumn. Treat every hill as ungroomed.
